S3.SS2: 3.2 Guidance Strength The coefficient \omega controls how far guidance extrapolates beyond the unguided prediction. Fixed strength. A constant \omega is used for every token within a given evaluation setting (Appendix B.4 ). Adaptive strength. LoopCD can adjust \omega at each token using the uncertainty of the unguided prediction. Let p_{R,(1)} and p_{R,(2)} be the two largest token probabilities in p_{R}=\operatorname{softmax}(z_{R}) . We set \omega=\omega_{\max}\bigl[1-(p_{R,(1)}-p_{R,(2)})\bigr], (4) where \omega_{\max} is the maximum strength. The rule approaches this maximum as the two leading probabilities become equal and reduces guidance as one candidate becomes dominant. The probability margin measures the uncertainty between the leading candidates directly, without computing entropy over the full vocabulary. LoopCD-Logits already computes the unguided logits z_{R} needed by the adaptive rule. Applying the same rule to LoopCD-Hidden would require a coda and head pass on h_{R} to obtain p_{R} , followed by another pass on h^{\prime} . We therefore use fixed and adaptive strength for LoopCD-Logits, and fixed strength for LoopCD-Hidden.
A2.SS1: B.1 Model configurations and paired comparisons Huginn is evaluated at both R=16 and R=32 ; the Ouro-Thinking checkpoints are used for mathematical reasoning and the Ouro base checkpoints for the other tasks. Looped-Qwen3 utilizes a frozen Qwen3-4B checkpoint with damped recurrent updates applied to a four-layer middle window (detailed in Appendix A.2 and Table A1 ). To ensure rigorous paired comparisons, a LoopCD run and its unguided baseline always share the identical checkpoint, prompt, shot count, generation limit, stopping rule, answer extractor, and evaluator. Recurrent depths are also strictly matched, except in explicit ablation studies comparing standard and reduced budgets. For the reduced-budget study, standard-budget baselines average repeated logit runs where available, while hidden-state runs are paired with their own dedicated baselines.
A2.SS2: B.2 Benchmarks and table conventions All reported scores are percentages. A subscript on a guided score denotes its signed percentage-point change ( \Delta ) from the strictly matched unguided baseline. The “Mean \Delta ” aggregates these changes with equal weight across the specific columns relevant to each evaluation suite. Multiple-choice benchmarks. Evaluated on ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy ( Clark et al., 2018 ), HellaSwag ( Zellers et al., 2019 ), WinoGrande ( Sakaguchi et al., 2020 ), PIQA ( Bisk et al., 2020 ), SciQ ( Welbl et al., 2017 ), and MMLU ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ). Candidates are scored by likelihood using the language model evaluation harness ( Gao et al., 2023 ). Greedy generation. Evaluated on HumanEval ( Chen et al., 2021 ), MBPP ( Austin et al., 2021 ), GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ), and MMLU-Pro ( Wang et al., 2024 ) with greedy decoding. Code generation is assessed via EvalPlus ( Liu et al., 2023 ) using both base and extended tests. GSM8K-CoT uses a strict-match extractor for the #### N format. Mathematical reasoning. Evaluated on AIME 2024 ( HuggingFaceH4, 2025 ), AIME 2025 ( OpenCompass, 2025 ) (30 problems each, integer matching), and the 674-problem English mathematics subset of OlympiadBench ( He et al., 2024 ) (symbolic equivalence). Each AIME set combines parts I and II of that year’s examination. We estimate pass@1 and pass@10 separately from 16 sampled solutions per problem using the standard unbiased estimator ( Chen et al., 2021 ; Zhu et al., 2025a ).

A2.SS4: B.4 Strengths and reference states Hyperparameters are determined via screening sweeps prior to full-suite evaluations (see Appendix G.1 , Figures 9 , and 10 ). Table A4 records the selected values for experiments at standard recurrent depth. Regarding strength-allocation strategies, we evaluate both fixed and adaptive strengths for regular-depth logit-space setups (multiple-choice scoring, greedy generation, and reasoning on Ouro-Thinking and Looped-Qwen3). Conversely, fixed strength alone is applied to all hidden-state configurations and to all experiments operating under a reduced recurrent depth. For LoopCD-Logits, the fixed strength ( \omega ) is 0.5 for multiple-choice scoring. For answer and code generation, it is 0.3 for Ouro and Looped-Qwen3 and 0.2 for Huginn. Reasoning strengths and adaptive caps ( \omega_{\max} ) are listed in Table A4 . For LoopCD-Hidden, the reference state ( h_{b} ) is chosen with the model’s initialization in mind (Appendix E.1 ). Parcae-1.3B has a deterministic prelude, so its contrast uses h_{1} at R=8 with \omega=1.0 . Huginn starts from Gaussian noise; after its burn-in phase, multiple-choice scoring uses h_{6} at R=32 and h_{7} at R=16 , both with \omega=0.5 . Generation uses h_{7} and h_{6} at those respective depths, with \omega=0.3 . Reduced-depth experiments use the distinct settings in Table A8 .
